record.title: Conjecture on congruences for partitions with distinct even parts
record.statement:
Let $ped(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which the even parts are distinct. **Congruence conjecture.** For each nonnegative integer $n$,

$$
ped(225n+43)\equiv 0\pmod{192},\qquad ped(225n+88)\equiv 0\pmod{192},
$$

$$
ped(225n+133)\equiv 0\pmod{192},\qquad ped(225n+223)\equiv 0\pmod{192}.
$$

These are proposed divisibility congruences for the partition function $ped(n)$, strengthening the preceding congruence results modulo $24$. Their status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Hemjyoti Nath, “New congruences for partitions where the even parts are distinct”, arXiv:2403.16735 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16735

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Enumerative recurrence conjecture for generalized stack-sortable permutations
record.statement:
For positive integers $t$ and $n$, let $\operatorname{Sort}_{t,n}(123,132)$ be the set of length-$n$ permutations that are $t$-stack-sortable under $s_{123,132}$. **Enumerative recurrence conjecture.** For any positive integer $t$ and $n\geq2t+1$,

- if $n$ is odd, then

$$
\lvert\operatorname{Sort}_{t,n}(123,132)\rvert=\frac{n+3}{2}\lvert\operatorname{Sort}_{t,n-2}(123,132)\rvert;
$$

- if $n$ is even, then

$$
\lvert\operatorname{Sort}_{t,n}(123,132)\rvert=\frac{n+4}{2}\lvert\operatorname{Sort}_{t,n-2}(123,132)\rvert.
$$

This predicts an explicit length recurrence for the enumerator of $t$-stack-sortable permutations under the specified generalized stack-sorting map; the source provides no resolution status.
record.source_name: Owen Zhang, “The Order of the (123, 132)-Avoiding Stack Sort”, arXiv:2405.01854 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.01854

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: Huh–Matherne–Mészáros–St. Dizier's Lorentzian conjecture for normalized Schubert polynomials
record.statement:
Let $w\in S_n$, let $\mathfrak{S}_w(x)$ be the Schubert polynomial indexed by $w$, and let $N$ be the normalization operator on monomials, defined by

$$
N(x^\alpha)=\frac{x_1^{\alpha_1}}{\alpha_1!}\cdots\frac{x_m^{\alpha_m}}{\alpha_m!}.
$$

A homogeneous polynomial is **Lorentzian** when its support is M-convex and every quadratic form obtained by differentiating it $d-2$ times has at most one positive eigenvalue. **Huh–Matherne–Mészáros–St. Dizier's conjecture.** For any $w\in S_n$, the polynomial $N(\mathfrak{S}_w(x))$ is Lorentzian. This conjecture extends the known result for permutations avoiding the patterns $1432$ and $1423$; the paper proves it when the corresponding Grothendieck polynomial is zero-one, giving partial confirmation, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Yiming Chen, Neil J. Y. Fan and Zelin Ye, “Zero-one Grothendieck Polynomials”, arXiv:2405.05483 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05483

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: The quadratic union-closure conjecture for the constructed family
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the family and $cl(\mathcal{S})$ its union closure, defined by $A\in cl(\mathcal{S})$ if and only if $A$ is the union of some subfamily of $\mathcal{S}$. Let $n$ denote the parameter used in the construction. **The quadratic union-closure conjecture.** For $x\geq 5$,

$$
|cl(\mathcal{S})|=\frac{23}{32}n^2+\frac{35}{8}n-21.
$$

The supplied context does not state whether this formula has been proved or remains open; its status is therefore left open.
record.source_name: Kengbo Lu and Abigail Raz, “Note on the union-closed sets conjecture and Reimer's average set size theorem”, arXiv:2405.10639 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.10639

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: Wilf-equivalence conjecture for the 13 pattern sets in Corollary 3
record.statement:
Let the $13$ pattern sets be the sets referred to in Corollary~, and let $\{13452,23451\}$ be represented by the partially ordered pattern (POP) shown in the source. **Wilf-equivalence conjecture.** The $13$ pattern sets in Corollary~ are Wilf-equivalent to $\{13452,23451\}$.

The conjecture proposes a common Wilf-equivalence class for the listed pattern sets and the displayed POP. The source gives no resolution of this claim.

record.title: The spherical E1a doubling conjecture for minimally rigid graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a minimally rigid graph, and let $G'$ be obtained from $G$ by a 1-extension of type E1a. Let $\mathbf{c}^{\circ}_{2}(G)$ denote the spherical realization count. **The spherical E1a doubling conjecture.** Then

$$
\frac{\mathbf{c}^{\circ}_{2}(G')}{\mathbf{c}^{\circ}_{2}(G)}=2.
$$

The claim extends the observed factor-two behavior to spherical realizations; the supplied text reports it for graphs with at most 13 vertices but does not establish the unrestricted statement.
record.source_name: Georg Grasegger, “Explorations on the number of realizations of minimally rigid graphs”, arXiv:2502.04736 (2025).

record.title: Saikia and Sarma's congruence conjectures for overcubic partition triples
record.statement:
Let $\overline{bt}(n)$ denote the number of overcubic partition triples of $n$.

**Saikia and Sarma's conjecture.** For $n,\alpha\geq 0$,

$$
\overline{bt}(144n+42)\equiv 0\pmod{384},\qquad
\overline{bt}\bigl(2^{\alpha}(72n+21)\bigr)\equiv 0\pmod{128},\qquad
\overline{bt}\bigl(2^{\alpha}(72n+69)\bigr)\equiv 0\pmod{128}.
$$

This is the second conjectured infinite family of congruences mentioned in the supplied text; its resolution is not given.
record.source_name: Jiayu Chen, Jing Jin and Olivia X. M. Yao, “Proofs of two conjectures on congruences of overcubic partition triples”, arXiv:2504.06941 (2025).

record.title: Contiguity conjecture for unions of random perfect matchings
record.statement:
Let $n$ be even and let $d\in[3,n-3]$. For each even $n$, fix a set $A_n$ of $d$-regular graphs on $n$ vertices. Let $G(n,1)\oplus\dotsb\oplus G(n,1)$ denote the disjoint union of $d$ random perfect matchings.

**Random matching decomposition conjecture.** The event that the disjoint union belongs to $A_n$ holds with high probability if and only if the event that a uniform random $d$-regular graph belongs to $A_n$ holds with high probability:

$$
G(n,1)\oplus\dotsb\oplus G(n,1)\in A_n\text{ with high probability}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G(n,d)\in A_n\text{ with high probability}.
$$

The paper proves one implication for $d\le n^{1/10}$ and states that, more generally, both the implication and its converse are believed to hold throughout $d\in[3,n-3]$.
record.source_name: Lawrence Hollom, Lyuben Lichev, Adva Mond, Julien Portier and Yiting Wang, “Monotonicity and decompositions of random regular graphs”, arXiv:2505.22875 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.22875

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

record.title: A 7-adic recurrence congruence for generalized Frobenius partitions with parameter 6
record.statement:
For integers $\alpha>0$, $\beta\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, and $n$ satisfying

$$
\beta^2-6\equiv 12n\pmod{7^{2\alpha-1}},
$$

**The recurrence congruence conjecture.**

$$
c\psi_{6,\beta}(49n+24-4\beta^2)\equiv x_\alpha\,c\psi_{6,\beta}(n)\pmod{7^\alpha},
$$

where $x_\alpha$ is a constant depending on $\alpha$. This predicts a family of 7-adic congruence relations among generalized Frobenius partition functions and is presented as another example of the congruence phenomenon discussed in the paper. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Rong Chen and Xiao-Jie Zhu, “Correspondence among congruence families for generalized Frobenius partitions via modular permutations”, arXiv:2506.16823 (2026).

record.title: Czap, Przybyło and Škrabul'áková's bipartite 1-planar graph size conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite $1$-planar graph with partite sets $X$ and $Y$, where $|X|$ and $|Y|$ are integers satisfying

$$
|X|\geq 3\quad\text{and}\quad |Y|\geq 6|X|-12.
$$

**Czap, Przybyło and Škrabul'áková's conjecture.** The size of $G$ satisfies

$$
|E(G)|\leq 2|V(G)|+4|X|-12.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the lower bound constructed by Czap, Przybyło and Škrabul'áková is optimal when the partite sets have these sizes. The claim concerns the extremal size of bipartite $1$-planar graphs with prescribed partite-set sizes and remains unresolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Guiping Wang, “A note on the sizes of bipartite 1-planar graphs”, arXiv:2507.19762 (2025).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

record.title: Schmeichel–Hakimi conjecture on exceptional planar graphical sequences
record.statement: A graphical sequence is **planar graphical** if it is the degree sequence of a planar graph. Using the shorthand $a^bc^d$ for $b$ repetitions of $a$ followed by $d$ repetitions of $c$, consider the sequences $5^{13}3^1$, $7^15^{17}$, and $7^35^{17}$. **Schmeichel–Hakimi conjecture.** None of these three sequences is planar graphical. The source states that these are the three unresolved cases remaining after their theorem, so the conjecture is open.
record.source_name: Jorik Jooken, “Computer-assisted graph theory: a survey”, arXiv:2508.20825 (2025).

record.title: Characteristic-zero exterior shifting conjecture for surface triangulations
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a triangulation on $n$ vertices of a connected compact surface without boundary, and let $\Delta^{ex}$ denote exterior algebraic shifting over a field of characteristic zero.

**Characteristic-zero exterior shifting conjecture.**

$$
\{1,3,n\}\in\Delta^{ex}(K).
$$

This conjecture is stated as a sufficient condition for the barycentric subdivision conjecture. The source gives no resolution; it attributes the related rigidity context to Bulavka (2023).
record.source_name: Denys Bulavka, Eran Nevo and Yuval Peled, “The typical algebraic shifting of a surface”, arXiv:2509.26525 (2025).
record.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2025).

record.title: Heron–Rota–Welsh log-concavity conjecture for Whitney numbers of matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r(M)$, with characteristic polynomial

$$
\chi_M(\lambda)=\sum_{i=0}^{r(M)}w_i(M)\lambda^{r(M)-i}.
$$

The integers $w_i(M)$ are the Whitney numbers of the first kind. **Heron–Rota–Welsh conjecture.** The sequence

$$
\{|w_i(M)|\}_{i=0}^{r(M)}
$$

of absolute values of the coefficients of $\chi_M(\lambda)$ is log-concave. This stronger conjecture was resolved in 2018 by Adiprasito, Huh, and Katz, whose results imply the earlier unimodality conjecture.
record.source_name: M. Ram Murty and Sunil Naik, “Brun's inequality for a geometric lattice”, arXiv:2510.07046 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07046

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2025). “This conjecture was resolved in 2018 by Adiprasito-Huh-Katz , one of the works for which J. Huh has been awarded Fields medal in 2022.”

record.title: Conjectural enumeration of translation-equivalence classes of intervals
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{WA}_{n}^{132}$ be the set of well-aligned pairs avoiding the pattern $132$. Consider the equivalence relation identifying pairs whose Bruhat intervals are translation-equivalent: $(v,w)\sim(v',w')$ when the intervals $[v,w]$ and $[v',w']$ are translation-equivalent. **Enumeration conjecture.** The total number of equivalence classes of translation-equivalent intervals in $\operatorname{WA}_{n}^{132}$ is given by OEIS sequence A111088.

The sequence A111088 counts circular planar electrical networks, but the source supplies no proof of the proposed enumeration.

record.title: Kantor's flag-transitive generalized quadrangle conjecture
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a finite flag-transitive generalized quadrangle. A generalized quadrangle is **classical** when it is one of the standard generalized quadrangles arising from a classical polar space; two generalized quadrangles are considered equivalent up to duality when points and lines may be interchanged. **Kantor's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{S}$ is not a classical generalized quadrangle, then, up to duality, $\mathcal{S}$ is the unique generalized quadrangle of order $(3,5)$ or the generalized quadrangle of order $(15,17)$ arising from the Lunelli--Sce hyperoval. This is presented as part of the outstanding classification problem for flag-transitive generalized polygons; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Tao Feng and Koen Thas, “Ealy's conjecture in odd characteristic”, arXiv:2511.21791 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.21791

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2025). “Unfortunately no such results are available in the ``odd" case, and consequently the odd case is still open after almost 50 years.”

record.title: Vexillary partial permutation minimality conjecture for real matrix Schubert varieties
record.statement: Let $\omega$ be a partial permutation, and let $X_\omega\subset\mathfrak{M}_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the corresponding open dense regular part of the real matrix Schubert variety. A partial permutation is **vexillary** if it avoids the $2143$-pattern. **Vexillary partial permutation minimality conjecture.** If $\omega$ is a vexillary partial permutation, then $X_\omega\subset\mathfrak{M}_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$ is minimal. The theorem preceding this conjecture proves the necessary direction for non-vexillary partial permutations; the conjecture asserts that vexillarity is also sufficient for minimality, linking pattern avoidance with the mean-curvature geometry of matrix Schubert varieties.
record.source_name: Jaehoon Lee, Sangwoo Park and Eungbeom Yeon, “On stationary real matrix Schubert varieties”, arXiv:2512.03480 (2025).

record.title: The two-prime -primitive number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct primes, and let $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$. Consider natural numbers of the form

$$
n=p^xq^y.
$$

A natural number is **$\Delta$-primitive** if it has the $\Delta$ property and is not obtained by multiplying a smaller $\Delta$-primitive number by a nontrivial square. **Two-prime $\Delta$-primitive number conjecture.** If $n$ is $\Delta$-primitive, then

$$
n\in\{24,40\}.
$$

The claim is motivated by experimental evidence and by the preceding theorem, which establishes the corresponding classification for numbers of the form $p^kq$; the general two-prime case remains open.
record.source_name: Victor N. Schvöllner, “The Δ property: a bridge between split graphs and Number Theory”, arXiv:2605.25264 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25264

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2026).

record.title: Faron–Postle Ore-degree conjecture for line-graph cliques
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. For a non-empty subgraph $H$ of $G$, define its **Ore-degree in $G$** by

$$
\sigma_G(H):=\max_{xy\in E(H)}(\deg_G(x)+\deg_G(y)),
$$

with $\sigma_G(H)=0$ when $H$ is empty. Suppose that $H$ is a bipartite subgraph of $G$ and that $E(H)$ forms a clique in $L(G)^2$. **Faron–Postle conjecture.** Then

$$
|E(H)|\le \frac{1}{4}\sigma_G(H)^2.
$$

This stronger Ore-degree statement implies the Faudree–Gyárfás–Schelp–Tuza strong clique index conjecture. The paper proves a substantial partial result with coefficient $\frac{620}{1987}$, but the conjectured coefficient $\frac14$ remains open.
record.source_name: Hitesh Kumar, Bojan Mohar and Shivaramakrishna Pragada, “An improved bound for the strong clique index of graphs”, arXiv:2607.02698 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02698

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2026). “This was later established by Chung, Gy\'{a}rf\'{a}s, Tuza and Trotter .”

record.title: Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Burness's unrestricted regularity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite almost simple group with socle $G_0$, and let a non-standard subgroup mean a subgroup whose associated primitive action is non-standard in the sense defined in the source. **Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Burness's conjecture.** Every $7$-tuple of non-standard subgroups of $G$ is regular.

This conjecture asks whether the conjugacy condition in Cameron's solved formulation can be removed, and is presented as a conjecture from Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Burness (2024).
record.source_name: Timothy C. Burness and Lei Wang, “On the regularity of irreducible subgroups of finite classical groups”, arXiv:2607.03307 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03307

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2026). “The precise form of the conjecture was established in later work by Burness et al. , working extensively with a powerful probabilistic approach for bounding the base size of a finite permutation group, which was originally introduced in .”
